Hi Graziele, this is Doctor Carter. Thank you for the plan. It looks great. One small change: our flight arrives at nine, not at eight. Could the driver come at nine? And one more thing: Doctor Lee doesn't eat meat. Thank you for the lunch. See you on Thursday.

Hi Graziele, it is Ana. A quick tip about offers. When you decide to help in the moment, say I'll. I'll call the driver. I'll get you a coffee. I'll send the email now. I'll is short for I will. After I'll, use the simple verb, with no to. Keep it simple. You will do great.

Graziele explains the plan for the visit. First, the driver will meet the doctors at the airport. Then, he will take them to the hotel. Next, Graziele will meet them at reception with their badges. After that, she will give them a tour of the hospital. Finally, they will have lunch with the team.
